title: Training and Support for Professionals in Special Needs Sector
what_it_is: Training and Support for Professionals in Special Needs Sector

sections.label: Special needs sector professionals
sections.summary: About 1,900 professionals, including teachers, social workers, psychologists and therapists, work in EIPIC and SPED schools.

sentences.text: The following question stood in the name of  Ms Rahayu Mahzam –  2  To ask the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) what is the current total number of professionals, such as teachers and social workers, who are in the special needs sector; (b) what training and professional development programmes are available for the professionals in this sector; and (c) what are the support structures in place to ensure that these professionals do not suffer from burnout or are able to cope with the stresses of the job.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: There are about 1,900 professionals working in the Early Intervention Programme for Infants and Children (EIPIC) and in Special Education (SPED) schools today.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: These include teachers, social workers, psychologists and therapists.

sections.label: Disability sector training programmes
sections.summary: SSI and NIE provide continuing education and training programmes for professionals in the disability sector.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: To complement this, the Social Service Institute (SSI) and the National Institute of Education (NIE) provide professionals in the disability sector with continuing education and training (CET) programmes.

sections.label: Subsidised self-care courses
sections.summary: Government-subsidised courses teach skills such as mindfulness and self-care, funded through grants like the Local Training Grant.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: There are also courses that equip professionals with skills to cope with the demands of their work, such as mindfulness and self-care practices.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: These courses are subsidised by the Government, through grants, such as the Local Training Grant from the voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs)-Charities Fund.

sections.label: Sabbatical Leave Scheme
sections.summary: NCSS introduced the Sabbatical Leave Scheme in 2008, giving nominated professionals 10 weeks paid leave and course sponsorship; about 170 have benefited.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Aside from self-care courses run by the SSI, NCSS also introduced the Sabbatical Leave Scheme in 2008 to help reduce burnout in professionals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Through this scheme, social service professionals nominated by their organisations receive funding from NCSS that provides them with 10 weeks of paid leave to recharge and refresh themselves, as well as sponsorship for professional development courses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: To date, about 170 professionals have benefited from this scheme.

sections.label: EIPIC back-room work day
sections.summary: Some EIPIC centres give teachers a one-day reprieve from direct intervention for back-room administrative tasks such as programme planning.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Some EIPIC centres have also structured the work week such that teachers have a one-day reprieve from direct intervention, to work on back-room administrative tasks, such as programme planning.
